title: Bound Triton specialization fan-out for dynamic tensor extents

source.title: triton.jit — Triton documentation
source.claim_scope: The API exposes do_not_specialize and do_not_specialize_on_alignment controls; whether using them improves end-to-end search cost without unacceptable runtime loss must be measured per kernel.

implementation_recipe: Classify scalar kernel arguments as semantic compile-time constants, launch meta-parameters, or runtime extents before starting a parameter sweep.
Keep only values required for unrolling or static layout as constexpr; screen do_not_specialize and do_not_specialize_on_alignment for variable extents.
Count process-local compiled specialization signatures across the frozen shape set instead of inferring cache behavior from source annotations.
Prefer the lower-fan-out form when its measured steady-state regression stays within the predeclared tolerance.
validation_recipe: Use identical launch geometry and paired alternating timing for specialized and runtime-extent forms.
Record correctness on anchor and edge shapes, specialization count, compile-path wall time, and steady-state latency separately.
Treat persistent disk-cache timing as non-cold unless the experiment explicitly owns and clears an isolated cache directory.
Remeasure exact launch geometry on the target architecture even when specialization control transfers.
expected_bottleneck_shifts: Fewer compiled variants reduce candidate turnaround and persistent-cache growth across variable shapes.
Suppressing value or alignment specialization can slightly reduce steady-state code quality, so agent throughput and kernel latency become an explicit tradeoff.
failure_modes: Removing a constexpr annotation but leaving implicit value or alignment specialization active.
Counting the outer device-cache tuple rather than compiled signatures and concluding that fan-out did not change.
Clearing a shared compiler cache destructively or comparing a cold path against a warm path without labeling it.
Carrying a proxy GPU's winning tile or warp count onto the target architecture.
scope_limits: Lower specialization count does not prove lower production latency.
A proxy architecture can validate workflow mechanics but cannot qualify target-architecture launch parameters.

candidate_archetypes.name: runtime extent with bounded specialization
candidate_archetypes.template: Hold the kernel math and launch geometry fixed, make dynamic extents non-specializing, then accept only if specialization count falls and paired steady-state latency stays within the frozen tolerance.
